keychainAsking: macOS is asking whether Leafen may use your keychain. Answer it there to go on.

appUpdate.ready: Leafen {{version}} is ready. It applies when you restart the app.
appUpdate.securityReady: A security update, Leafen {{version}}, is ready. Restart the app to apply it.
appUpdate.available: Leafen {{version}} is out. Update it from the Microsoft Store, or download the new zip.
appUpdate.securityAvailable: A security update, Leafen {{version}}, is out. Update it from the Microsoft Store, or download the new zip.
appUpdate.rolledBack: Leafen {{version}} didn’t start, so the app rolled back to the previous version and the data from before the update.

serverKeyChanged.title: This server’s key changed
serverKeyChanged.body: {{host}} answered as a different server than the one this app remembered. Someone may be impersonating its address to read your connection. Trust the new server only if you’re sure its administrator reinstalled it without its backup.
serverKeyChanged.unvouched: {{host}} answered with a certificate the server didn’t vouch for. Someone may be impersonating its address to read your connection. Ask its administrator before continuing.
serverKeyChanged.back: Go back to this device’s Leafen

serverMoved.text: This server’s data moved to another server. Changes made here aren’t kept.
serverMoved.textNoAddress: This server’s data moved to another server. Changes made here aren’t kept. Open Leafen at the address of the server that took the data over.
serverMoved.paused: This server can’t reach its backup location right now, and its standby may take over, so it isn’t accepting changes until it can.
serverMoved.standby: This is a standby server: it follows another server, and its own data is replaced when it takes over.
serverMoved.standbyOf: This is the standby server of {{address}}: its own data is replaced when it takes over.
serverMoved.tookOver: This server isn’t responding, and its standby server {{address}} has taken over.
serverMoved.workspace: This workspace moved to another server and no longer accepts changes here.
serverMoved.workspaceSending: This workspace is moving to another server and isn’t accepting changes here.

properAddress.offer: This server now has a permanent address, {{address}}. This address still works here; continue there to use it from anywhere.
properAddress.failed: Couldn’t transfer the login. Try again, or log in there with a code.

addressHandoff.carried: Leafen moved to {{host}}; this device stayed logged in.
addressHandoff.passkey: Create a passkey for this address

openInApp.lead: If you have the Leafen app, you can open this page in it.
openInApp.homeScreen: To get notifications, add Leafen to your Home Screen: Safari’s Share → Add to Home Screen. The Home Screen Leafen keeps its own login, so it logs in with a code.
openInApp.homeScreenCode: In the Home Screen Leafen, enter {{code}} under “Log in with a code”. It works once, within 10 minutes.

localReach.loopbackOnly: Only this computer can open this address
localReach.homeOnly: Only devices on the same network can open this address.

startupRecovery.slowTitle: Leafen is taking longer than usual to start
startupRecovery.slowBody: It’s still starting and opens automatically once ready. If this persists, save the log or check the data folder.
startupRecovery.lockedTitle: Another program is using Leafen’s data
startupRecovery.lockedBody: Another Leafen, or a backup or sync app, may be holding it. Close that program, then try again.
startupRecovery.diskFullBody: Leafen needs room on the disk its data is on. Free some up, then try again.
startupRecovery.failedBody: Try again. If it keeps happening, save the log and send it to whoever helps you with Leafen.
startupRecovery.backup: The last backup was made {{when}}. Restoring it keeps the current data aside until the next backup, for up to 7 days, so the restore can be undone.
startupRecovery.noBackup: No backup is noted on this device. Save the log before changing anything in the data folder.
startupRecovery.secretPrompt: This backup is encrypted. Enter its recovery code or password.
startupRecovery.openFailed: The data folder couldn’t be opened
